scenes.text: If you hit this solid-looking black rock with a heavy hammer, it will shatter into a thousand tiny pieces, yet scientists prove it is actually a slowly moving liquid.
Known as tar pitch, this incredibly dense substance is over two hundred billion times thicker than water, meaning it flows at a speed so slow it seems completely frozen in time.
To test this mind-blowing property, a famous university experiment started in 1927 by placing the pitch in a glass funnel, and in almost a century, only nine drops have fallen.
Because a single drop takes a whole decade to fall, researchers keep missing the exact moment it happens, so would you have the patience to watch this, or should you follow for more?
